correctness.rationale: The sketched normal equation for unit A=(e1+e2)/sqrt2 and orthogonal response gives xhat=(gamma1²-gamma2²)/(gamma1²+gamma2²+2rho gamma1 gamma2), with rho the average of m independent uniform Hadamard pair-sign products. Conditioning on rho=a and isotropic Gaussian angle gives Z_a=cos(2theta)/(1+a sin(2theta)). For |a|<1 it has the stated arcsine CDF and bounded support (1-a²)^(-1/2); for a=±1 it equals a ratio of independent equal-variance normals and is standard Cauchy. The collision mass P(|rho|=1)=2^(1-m), verified independently via exact binomial weights through m=16; all other components have support bounded by T_m=m/(2sqrt(m-1)). Thus the exact two-sided tail above T_m is mass*2arctan(1/t)/pi, and integrability threshold p<1 follows for each finite m. Uniqueness a.s. holds also at rho=±1 because its Gram denominator is a nonzero squared Gaussian except on a null set.
residual_risks: The comparison of noncolliding support uses fixed finite m, not a uniform-in-m compact support bound.
